request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Small requested changes expanded into rewrites.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Compare the work with the request before responding.",
    "description": "Use for tasks.",
    "name": "scope-check"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "A skill can guide scope management."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":2,"justification":"\"Compare the work with the request before responding\" is a post-hoc check with no specified corrective action (e.g., revert unrequested edits, ask before expanding scope), so it doesn't reliably change future behavior."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The body is a content-free platitude that could apply to any task and gives no specific guidance tied to the scope-creep failure mode (e.g., limiting diff to the requested lines, flagging extra refactors)."},"trigger_quality":{"score":1,"justification":"The description \"Use for tasks.\" is not a real trigger — it fails to specify any condition distinguishing this skill from default behavior, so it would fire on everything or nothing predictably."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"The remedy text is fully generic and contains no project-specific nouns or evidence-specific details from the failure case."},"routing_fitness":{"score":2,"justification":"The routing rationale is circular (\"a skill can guide scope management\") and doesn't justify why a persistent skill file is cheaper or more appropriate than a lighter-weight reminder, given the vague, poorly-triggered content it delivers."}}

actionability.justification: "Compare the work with the request before responding" is a post-hoc check with no specified corrective action (e.g., revert unrequested edits, ask before expanding scope), so it doesn't reliably change future behavior.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The body is a content-free platitude that could apply to any task and gives no specific guidance tied to the scope-creep failure mode (e.g., limiting diff to the requested lines, flagging extra refactors).

leakage.justification: The remedy text is fully generic and contains no project-specific nouns or evidence-specific details from the failure case.

routing_fitness.justification: The routing rationale is circular ("a skill can guide scope management") and doesn't justify why a persistent skill file is cheaper or more appropriate than a lighter-weight reminder, given the vague, poorly-triggered content it delivers.

trigger_quality.justification: The description "Use for tasks." is not a real trigger — it fails to specify any condition distinguishing this skill from default behavior, so it would fire on everything or nothing predictably.
